title: Two groups, one species
hook: Animals that need mates to breed. Do small groups always grow back?

knows: populations level off when food runs out (logistic growth)
doesNotKnow: that some populations shrink when too small

misconception: Any population, however small, will grow back if left alone.
objective: The learner can explain that when animals need a minimum group size to find mates, a group below the threshold (40 of 50) shrinks to nothing while a group above it (60) grows to the limit of 1,000.

claims.text: In a strong Allee effect, a population below a critical size has negative growth and dies out, while one above it grows.
claims.source: Courchamp, Berec & Gascoigne, Allee Effects in Ecology and Conservation, Oxford University Press, 2008.

claims.text: Toy model dN/dt = 0.1 N (N/50 - 1)(1 - N/1000): a group that starts at 40 falls below 1 animal by year 54 and one that starts at 60 reaches about 1,000 (also 20 dies out by year 35, 80 reaches about 1,000).
claims.source: Demo.tsx Euler run, step 0.5 year, 60 years, drawn on the stage; node check in artifacts/scratch/w5life/allee2.mjs: 40 extinct year 54 (0.50 at year 60), 60 final 1000.00, 20 extinct year 35, 80 final 1000.00. Deterministic, no randomness.

claims.text: Model, as shown: before the prediction the stage reads "Toy: room for 1,000. Log scale."; the vertical axis is marked 1, 10, 100 and 1,000 at equal steps (a log scale); once unlocked a line marks the threshold of 50; a group that falls under 1 animal is reported as dying out; and the reveal says the threshold and rate are invented and that food limits growth at 1,000.

recall.question: Animals need a minimum group size to find mates. Two groups of the same species start, one just below that size and one just above. What happens?
options: The smaller dies out, the larger grows
recall.why: Below the threshold each animal finds fewer mates, so numbers fall; above it they grow. A threshold splits the same species into recover or vanish.
